notes: Check batch 2026-10-23-check-3: four skill runs (haiku-1, haiku-2, sonnet-1, sonnet-2), no opus, all rc 0, each model_id matching its tier (each transcript's assistant messages name only that model; claude-opus-5-5 appears only in the harness's prompt snapshot and request-shape entries), head 4215aa3 with uncommitted true and one skill_hash (d31ff0b2...). git diff d04061d -- idiomatic-elixir/ shows only the uncommitted new rule "Break a `->` clause whose pattern and body together pass 70 characters" (SKILL.md, between the do:/do-end rule and the pipeline rule); it replaces check-2's "Keep a `->` clause on one line only when its pattern and body are each one plain term". Every transcript contains its sentence "fit in 70 characters, not counting indentation", so the runs read it. Each run made one Read, of SKILL.md, and no reference file; expected reads is none beyond SKILL.md, so all four meet it. In the scratch folder all four files pass mix format --check-formatted and compile with elixirc --warnings-as-errors (Elixir 1.20.3). Doctests: haiku-1 2 of 2, haiku-2 1 of 1, sonnet-1 3 of 3, sonnet-2 3 of 3.

New rule "Break a `->` clause whose pattern and body together pass 70 characters", graded against its text (deciding sentence: "A clause of `case`, `cond`, `with ... else` or `receive` stays on one line while its pattern, the `->` and its body together fit in 70 characters, not counting indentation.") and the case's bullet. Runs violating: 0 of 4. Runs exercising it: 4 of 4. Every clause in the batch is a case clause; there is no cond, receive or with ... else, and no fn argument with ->. Every one-line clause measured after its indentation; none passes 70. The longest per run, verbatim: haiku-1 line 134 (58): {:error, _reason} -> {:error, {:invalid_field, "created"}}; haiku-2 line 127 (58): the same text; sonnet-1 line 165 (66): {:ok, value} when is_binary(value) and value != "" -> {:ok, value}, and line 173 (66): {:ok, value} when is_integer(value) and value >= 0 -> {:ok, value}; sonnet-2 line 179 (70): {:ok, amount} when is_integer(amount) and amount >= 0 -> {:ok, amount}, exactly at the limit, which the text's "fit in 70 characters" allows, so clean (one character more and sonnet-2 would be violated). Broken clauses: only haiku-1's checked_field/3 (lines 114-120) and haiku-2's field/3 (lines 138-144) break, each on a clause whose one-line form would pass 70 ({:ok, value} -> if valid?.(value), do: {:ok, value}, else: {:error, {:invalid_field, key}}); in both every clause of that case is broken and a blank line separates the two clauses (haiku-1 line 117, haiku-2 line 141). sonnet-1 and sonnet-2 break no clause. Under check-2's replaced rule, sonnet-1's and sonnet-2's guarded one-line clauses (sonnet-1 lines 165, 173, 182, 190; sonnet-2 lines 163, 172, 179) would have been violations; under the length rule they are clean.

Unchanged rules, graded to the 2026-10-23 standard. Head-rule bullets, violating runs out of 4. (1) The parsing head matches the keys it requires with a clause below: haiku-2, sonnet-1 and sonnet-2 match id, type, created and data in parse/1 with def parse(_payload), do: {:error, :invalid_payload} below; haiku-1 matches only "type" (line 91: def parse(%{"type" => type} = payload) when is_binary(type) do) and reads id, created and data in the body with the Map.fetch-based checked_field/3, which names each missing or invalid key and raises nothing. The 2026-10-23 baseline grade put the same shape (baseline-opus-1) as a missed check with the rule clean, because nothing the rule forbids appears; graded the same here, so the check is missed and the verdict clean. (2) No selecting pattern moved into a body: 0 of 4. (3) Clutter: 0 of 4; the type mappers and data dispatchers match literals and take data whole, and the wrapped parse/1 heads (haiku-2 lines 76-77, sonnet-1 lines 101-102, sonnet-2 lines 102-103) move only the guard.

Closest calls. Match every expected shape: sonnet-1 line 127, defp parse_data(_payment_type, data), do: parse_payment(data), parses every atom other than :refund_created as a payment, the shape check-2 graded violated in both Sonnet runs and 2026-10-22-d before it, so violated; sonnet-2 now has three explicit parse_data/2 clauses (lines 127, 129, 136) and is clean. The type mappers' catch-alls in haiku-2 (line 92), sonnet-1 (line 115) and sonnet-2 (line 116) also receive a non-string type ("type" => 123 gives {:unsupported_event, 123}, verified), checks only as before; haiku-1 guards is_binary(type) in the head and gives :invalid_payload. Atoms: haiku-1 maps types through a literal @event_types map (lines 58-62) read with Map.fetch (line 107), graded clean as 2026-10-22-b and 2026-10-22-d graded the same shape. Read required keys: Map.get appears only in optional readers (haiku-1 line 124, haiku-2 line 148, sonnet-1 lines 180 and 188, sonnet-2 line 170) for keys their structs leave out of @enforce_keys, allowed as before. Comments: haiku-1 lines 92-93 and haiku-2 line 78 say why the type is checked before the fields, so clean. haiku-2's comment says an unknown type is reported "even if its data is malformed", but non-map data never reaches parse_type/1 (the is_map(data) guard sends it to :invalid_payload, verified); the comment holds for malformed fields inside a map, so not counted. Naming: sonnet-2 line 104 rebinds type to the parsed atom and line 106 rebinds data to the parsed struct, allowed as before; haiku-2's kind and object, and haiku-1's event_data and valid?, not counted. Outside the list: haiku-1 (lines 114, 116) and haiku-2 (lines 138, 140) put an if inside a case, counted under Keep functions short as in check-2 and 2026-10-23.

Probe of 24 payloads, run in the scratch folder against each compiled file. In all four: an unknown type gives {:unsupported_event, type}; a known type without amount gives {:missing_field, "amount"}; a string or nil amount gives {:invalid_field, "amount"}; refunds without refund_id or payment_id name that field; a string or out-of-range created gives {:invalid_field, "created"}; a non-map payload gives :invalid_payload. Differences: haiku-1 names a missing or ill-typed id, created or data ({:missing_field, "id"}, {:invalid_field, "data"}), where the others give :invalid_payload; a negative amount is accepted by haiku-1 and haiku-2 and rejected by the Sonnet runs; a missing customer_email is accepted by haiku-1 only; sonnet-2 rejects payment.failed with failure_reason nil ({:invalid_field, "failure_reason"}), so the prompt's example shape fails as a failed payment; a non-string type gives :invalid_payload in haiku-1 and {:unsupported_event, 123} in the others.

Compared with check-2 (same head, the replaced -> rule): Read required keys moves from Haiku violated to clean (no bracket reads after a head match); Match every expected shape stays Sonnet violated (sonnet-1 only, sonnet-2 now clean); the -> rule, measured by its new text, is clean in both tiers where check-2's plain-term rule had Sonnet violated. Compared with the sixth sweep's skill runs (2026-10-23 at d04061d): Match every expected shape moves from Sonnet clean to violated; Comments moves from Sonnet violated to clean. The multi-clause rule, atoms, the with rule, the return-tuple rule, the struct rule and Naming stay clean in Haiku and Sonnet.
